behavioral_notes.observation: The single model where every cost and revenue line in Odoo lands: hr_timesheet, sale_timesheet, project, hr_expense, purchase and account all _inherit or post account.analytic.line records, grouped on account.analytic.account (the value unit: project/order/cost centre). _compute_debit_credit_balance aggregates line amounts (>=0 credit / <0 debit) per plan column, currency-converted to the company currency, to yield balance/debit/credit on the account. This is the support<->primary join point and is invisible in metadata.

Plans are not just a hierarchy: each ROOT plan materialises a real m2o column on every analytic.plan.fields.mixin model. The project root plan maps to the fixed 'account_id'; every other root plan gets a generated 'x_plan{id}_id' ir.model.fields column (created/renamed/dropped on plan create/write/unlink via _sync_plan_column, with a btree partial index). Sub-plans add non-stored related grouping fields (_hierarchy_name). account.analytic.account.write moves line data across columns via raw SQL UPDATE when a plan changes. Pure runtime schema mutation, not in static metadata.

A rules engine that pre-fills the analytic_distribution JSON on documents. _get_applicable_models matches by partner_id / partner_category_id / company_id (each optional, False = wildcard) and merges the matching models' distributions, skipping any whose root plan is already applied. This is how an invoice/SO/expense automatically inherits an analytic account from its partner without manual entry.

The reusable mixin every analytic-bearing document inherits. analytic_distribution is a Json map of 'comma-joined account ids' -> percentage; a GIN index on regexp_split_to_array(jsonb keys) makes 'which docs hit this account' searchable, and _read_group_groupby rewrites group-by-distribution into a per-account subquery. _validate_distribution enforces that mandatory plans sum to 100%, and _merge_distribution recombines partial ('__update__') edits proportionally. The split/validation logic lives entirely in Python.

8 JS files, 1 OWL component (AnalyticDistribution), 6 registry adds; bundles ['web.assets_backend', 'web.assets_backend_lazy', 'web.assets_unit_tests']. The AnalyticDistribution widget renders the plan columns dynamically and edits the distribution JSON inline.

classification.rationale: Analytic Accounting is the financial cost-aggregation BACKBONE of the value system, not a primary value-creating activity itself: it provides the dimensional ledger (analytic accounts/plans) onto which other modules post cost and revenue. It is value-model 'support' and activity_class 'support' under Stabell & Fjeldstad / Porter, mapping to APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (specifically 9.3 perform cost accounting / management accounting). Its defining role per PRIMARY_SUPPORT_INTEGRATION_AR.md: account.analytic.line is THE join where support costs meet primary-activity value. Support activities (HR labour via hr_timesheet, purchasing, expenses via hr_expense) post their costs as analytic lines onto the same account.analytic.account that primary activities (sale_timesheet revenue, project delivery) credit -- so profit-per-value-unit is computable. The dynamic plan columns and distribution model exist precisely to route every transaction's value into that shared vessel. It is the support<->primary integration vessel rather than a member of any single primary value configuration.
